attempted_claim: Let X = P(x,y) d/dx + Q(x,y) d/dy be a complex planar polynomial vector field with max(deg P, deg Q) = 4, gcd(P,Q) = 1 and finitely many affine singularities. Is it true that the sum of the degrees of all pairwise distinct irreducible invariant algebraic curves of X is at most 12, and that equality forces an explicit Darboux first integral of the form prod_i f_i^{lambda_i} with f_i Darboux polynomials and lambda_i in C? A complete answer is either a proof of the degree-sum bound with derivation of the Darboux integral in the extremal case from the extactic determinant and cofactor syzygies, or an explicit verified quartic counterexample with distinct irreducible invariant curves of total degree at least 13 with cofactors checked by X(f_i) = K_i f_i.
